newsitem.title: MONGOLIA: Mongolia gold output up 63 pct in first half 1997.
newsitem.headline: Mongolia gold output up 63 pct in first half 1997.

text.p: Mongolia's gold output in the first half of this year was 2,156.3 kg, up 63 percent compared to the first half of 1996, and gold output for 1997 would exceed targets, the Bank of Mongolia said on Wednesday.

"The gold output this year will go well beyond the planned 6.5 tonnes, perhaps up to eight tonnes," a central bank official said. Mongolia produced 5.2 tonnes of gold in 1996, up from 4.5 tonnes in 1995.
Gold production would leap this summer when the Bumbat hard rock gold mine, run by Canada-based Mongolia Gold Resources Inc and local company Mongol Alt, begins operating, the official said.
"Gold production will increase in the next few years and gold could be one of Mongolia's most important export items," central bank governor Unenbat said.
Mongolia's gold exports in 1996 totalled $60 million, representing 14.19 percent of total export income of $422.9 million last year, he said.
However, increases in gold production this year may not be matched by similar rises in gold export earnings because of low prices on the world market, he said.
Unenbat did not give exports for 1995, but estimates at the end of that year put the figure at about $50 million.
Mongolia has said it plans to increase gold production to 12 to 14 tonnes by the year 2000.
